approach.method_basis: The formal Anchor evolves molecular graphs from the current session’s accepted scores. A fixed count-fingerprint Gaussian process predicts fresh offspring; ten correlated function draws allocate purchases through sequential maxima, with a top-forty mean-rank restriction after three non-improving batches. Raw scores update the full training archive, greedy survivor population and quantile-based breeder.
approach.novelty: Replace only the Gaussian predictive law with an analytically marginalized Student-t process. A single random covariance scale is shared by every candidate in each function draw, while the predictive mean, count geometry and consumer stay fixed. This integrates scale uncertainty instead of fitting a nonlinear warp, jointly fitting model scalars, or applying a deterministic widening correction. Complete prospective prediction and endpoint gain are tested separately.

sources.finding: The conditional multivariate Student-t law retains a GP-form mean while its covariance depends on observed values. sources.title: Shah, Wilson and Ghahramani — Student-t Processes as Alternatives to Gaussian Processes (AISTATS 2014)

method_change.previous_method: Formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de uses a fixed normalized count-kernel Gaussian predictive function law in its unchanged graph-pool Thompson consumer.
method_change.proposed_method: The same conditional mean and count correlation geometry with a nu3 analytically marginalized shared-scale Student-t predictive law and row-shared inverse-Gamma draws.
method_change.rationale: A different fully specified probability law avoids nonconvex warp estimation while making no promise that uncertainty correction fixes allocation. Historical widening, joint point-fit and complete unit-warp adverse endpoints remain contrary evidence; the current test starts directly from its literal formal comparator.

hypothesis: At every original accepted-archive refit, replace the fixed Gaussian function law by the paper’s finite-variance Student-t process with prior nu=3 and one analytically integrated shared signal-plus-training-nugget scale. Use the same standardized labels z, C=KXX+0.05^2 I+j_train I, original Cholesky solution alpha=C^-1 z and raw predictive mean mu_y=mean(y)+scale(y) KqX alpha. Compute beta=z^T C^-1 z, d=nu+n, b=(nu+beta-2)/2 and r=(nu+beta-2)/(nu+n-2). The mathematical latent Schur covariance is S=Kqq-KqX C^-1 KXq; conditional covariance is rS, and conventional Student-t scale matrix is ((nu+beta-2)/(nu+n))S. Retain the Parent’s pool factorization F F^T=S+j_pool I, with its exact jitter ladder; call this explicitly logged numerical covariance S_eff. Every implemented draw and prospective marginal consistently uses S_eff, while analytic S and the stabilization difference are recorded separately. For each of the original ten independent normal rows Z_j draw one independent rho_j~InvGamma(d/2,b) and set draw_j=mu_y+scale(y)*sqrt(rho_j)*(Z_j F^T). One rho multiplies the entire ordered pool row, never one rho per coordinate; no extra query observation noise is added. Raw means and same-state gate membership remain exactly those of the original GP. Changed radial amplitudes relative to unchanged locations can change paid maxima, whose real accepted feedback can then alter later archives, survivors and breeding. Neither pair-mean ordering improvement nor an endpoint mediator is asserted.

finding_summary.headline: The Student-t law completed and improved paid predictive loss, but the endpoint score fell.
finding_summary.insights: Complete analytic integration removes a numerical-completeness explanation for this prediction-to-endpoint gap. It does not improve the predictive mean or its ordering: those are identical to the same-state GP by construction. The actual changed purchases entered later fits, survivor populations and breeding, but these associations do not establish why the endpoint fell. Full generating-parent gain decreased from 16.8912 to 14.4408 even as the number of parent-beating purchases rose; late generating-parent gain increased from 4.4024 to 4.8820. These quantities differ from incumbent gain, which simply telescopes to the endpoints. The molecular audit also shows broader small- and large-molecule tails and concentrated high-score families despite greater pooled scaffold richness. Such findings leave predictive-location models, proposal operators and the allocation consumer as distinct kinds of method that could address unchanged capabilities; they do not identify a successful next intervention or a chemical cause of the score change. The result applies to this fixed prior, host and finite Search panel. It neither refutes the whole Student-t approach nor redeems its two reserved follow-ups, and retained-component contribution gaps remain open.
finding_summary.results: All 435 pool laws and 4,350 prospective paid predictions passed their frozen numerical and identity checks. The new law changed 332 of 435 purchase sets and bought 973 molecules absent from the original GP choices on the same state. Its registered raw-unit pinball loss fell from 0.02061650 to 0.01931875, with a decrease in every task/seed cell. A Gaussian with the same conditional covariance scored 0.01931940, so nearly all of that diagnostic loss difference is also present without Student-t marginal shape. The joint radial law still changed 214 purchases relative to that Gaussian. The complete endpoint macro was 0.57280205 versus 0.60703032 for both the code Parent and formal Anchor, a difference of -0.03422826; the unchanged target was 0.60903032. Seed differences were -0.10038193, +0.01038540 and -0.01268826, with eight cell gains and seven losses. All protocol paired task-safety checks pass under their actual margins and standard errors. The primary predictive prediction is confirmed; the separate endpoint criterion is missed.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich, halogenated families retain reactive motifs and undefined stereochemistry, with broader small- and large-molecule tails.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers every supplied Search trajectory for n-c34780421617 and archived code Parent/formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de: five tasks times seeds 0/1/2. Actual file availability is 15/15 cells for each node. Separately, all six evaluator summaries and all thirty task entries report ok; each cell has evaluations 1..300, ten initial records and 290 accepted optimizer records, with unique recorded identities. Thus each node contributes 150 initial record occurrences and 4350 optimizer record occurrences, including 2175 late purchases (optimizer ordinals 146..290, evaluations 156..300). The frozen comparison independently declares child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds [0,1,2], and no profile mismatches. This is complete observed Child chemistry and complete descriptive Parent pairing, not a certificate of prospective model-law completeness or mechanism activation. No missing trajectory was treated as an empty molecular population. The same ten initial structures recur across the fifteen sessions; initial records are kept separate from new proposals. RDKit 2023.09.6 parses all saved records. The Child proposals are predominantly ring-bearing and aromatic, with amide/imide, amine, ether, halogen and heterocycle chemistry; 4171/4350 have rings and 3979/4350 have an aromatic atom. The supplied digest independently has ring-closure text rates 0.9080..0.9839 and aromatic-text rates 0.7046..0.9793 across tasks; these are text counters, not perceived ring counts. Ordinary medicinal-chemistry fragments coexist with N/O-halogen bonds, peroxides, small-ring aromatic topologies, large conjugated assemblies and simple fragments. These observations motivate questionable synthetic plausibility and weak drug-likeness as qualitative readings; they are not measured synthesis, stability, ADME or biological activity. Child optimizer heavy-atom quantiles (minimum, 10%, 25%, median, 75%, 90%, maximum) are 1,23,26,30,33.75,40,120; Parent values are 1,24,25,28,32,34,96. The separate <=5, <=6, >=50 and >50 counts are Child 162,177,298,291 versus Parent 91,98,46,44. For the 2175 late records they are 66,73,138,135 versus 33,36,3,3. The 150 initial occurrences have range 6..39 and 15 at <=6, with none at <=5 or >=50. These denominators and conventions must not be combined. The large Child tail is concentrated in one task and especially one seed, described below. Graph queries find N-halogen/O-halogen/peroxide motifs in 626/262/189 Child proposals versus 888/162/118 Parent proposals; individual categories can overlap. No proposal in either node has an atom with formal charge or an assigned tetrahedral centre. Yet 2453 Child and 2578 Parent proposals have at least one unassigned tetrahedral centre. Neutral SMILES do not establish solution protonation, and an unassigned centre does not establish that the compound was synthesized as a mixture. The Child has 21 structures with a carbon bonded to multiple halogens, so the observed chemistry does not support an absolute claim that this feature is unreachable. Typed/generic Bemis-Murcko scaffold counts over all 4350 optimizer occurrences are 1869/1222 distinct nonempty Child scaffolds and 1667/951 Parent scaffolds; empty acyclic scaffolds are excluded from those distinct counts and separately number 179/95 occurrences. This pooled richness coexists with concentrated high-score families within individual sessions. High/low deciles below mean exactly 29 records per seed, ordered only by saved score with evaluation-order ties, then pooled to 87 per task; they are not the global top 87 and do not rank algorithms. All fifteen audits retain full, initial, late, high- and low-decile denominators, tails, typed/generic scaffold counts and pairwise similarity statistics. Similarity is RDKit Tanimoto on unhashed radius-2 Morgan count fingerprints, without chirality or feature invariants, using every unordered distinct-record pair within a cell. It is reported before and after excluding molecules with <=6 heavy atoms, with both molecule and pair counts. This fragment-size exclusion is a diagnostic convention, not a chemical filter applied to the run. No cross-task pairwise similarity is inferred. The trajectories do not contain the same-state passive-choice identities needed for changed-versus-unchanged purchase strata; those strata are unavailable in this molecular audit and are not inferred from Child-versus-Parent differences. Complete trajectories do not fill that separate evidential gap. Chemistry associations do not explain a score change causally, certify any retained component, establish population benefit, or identify an absent target-required pharmacophore. The transferable gaps concern demonstrated output limitations and possible task-agnostic questions only. missing_features: The larger nitrogen-containing rings and multiple fusion patterns are not accompanied by conformational or synthetic evidence; a ring graph alone does not show a practically accessible structure.

The final seed-2 peroxide-containing example remains at 0.20968810837201093, so a relatively high observed label alone does not certify chemical robustness.

liabilities: The Child has 364/870 N-halogen records, 211/870 N-O single-bond records and 24/870 carbon-centred cumulated-double-bond records; these motif categories overlap and do not have a shared measured stability.
The <=6-heavy-atom tail expands to 83/870 from Parent 20/870. Six Child records have >=50 heavy atoms, three have >50, and Parent has neither tail. The separate boundary conventions matter.
Complex ring fusions, imines, aminal centres, N-F bonds and cyclic cumulenes make plausible synthesis and configuration uncertain despite accepted valence and nonzero labels.
missing_features: The generated high-score families do not demonstrate a consistent combination of defined stereochemistry and structurally conservative fluorination; 86/87 high-decile records have an unassigned tetrahedral centre and 62/87 contain an N-halogen bond.

Aromaticity is not universally required by the observed high labels, and the trajectories do not identify a missing target-specific scaffold or prove biological suitability of the nonaromatic families.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The three cited higher-label records score 0.4411698841689937, 0.695727406452767 and 0.6411928061142901. A duplicated, much larger carbonyl-rich scaffold scores 6.575321317730757e-32 and the isolated fluorine record 1.1043196211273875e-26. High within-cell deciles occupy 24..31 heavy atoms, whereas the low deciles contain 75 <=6-heavy-atom records and five >=50-heavy-atom records. The observed labels therefore distinguish both size extremes from the intermediate-size families, without making every intermediate structure chemically plausible. The cited cyclic cumulene-containing seed-1 molecule still scores 0.6835196781437569; this does not establish a feasible geometry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across 4350 Child optimizer records, 177 contain <=6 heavy atoms and 291 contain >50, compared with 98 and 44 in the paired Parent streams. The late 2175 records retain 73 and 135 such cases. These are record counts under separate, explicit thresholds; they do not establish that all small or large compounds are unsuitable.
transferable_gaps.gap: The observed generator does not reliably preserve a coherent molecular size scale while exploring new structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic development question is how local graph edits can preserve or deliberately change molecular size with meaningful context from the current session, rather than repeatedly producing tiny fragments or oversized assemblies. Any size policy would need its own prospective test; this assessment adds no filter.

transferable_gaps.evidence: N-halogen, O-halogen and peroxide queries match 626,262,189 Child proposals versus 888,162,118 Parent proposals. N-halogen and O-halogen motifs remain among high observed labels. Conversely, 21 Child structures already contain a multiply halogenated carbon, so absolute inability to generate that motif is not supported.
transferable_gaps.gap: Conventional functional groups are not consistently separated from chemically sensitive local bond environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could distinguish local bond-environment classes when proposing substitutions and preserve conventional carbon-bound alternatives as reachable options. Reactivity-aware proposal changes would require independent testing; these motif counts alone do not justify rejecting every member of a class or claim an endpoint gain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Both nodes have zero proposals with an assigned tetrahedral centre or nonzero atomic formal charge. At least one unassigned tetrahedral centre is perceived in 2453/4350 Child and 2578/4350 Parent proposals, including entire high-score subfamilies of amine-bearing rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify tetrahedral configuration or explicit charge even when its structures make those distinctions chemically relevant.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation could make stereochemical assignments and chemically supported ionization states explicit and maintain them through edits and identity handling. Neither the absent annotations nor this suggested capability imply that an unmeasured stereoisomer or protonation state would improve a score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Small rings of at most four atoms whose atoms are all aromatic occur in 184/4350 Child records versus 170/4350 Parent records. The Child also contains 316 records with a ring of at least nine atoms, compared with 162 Parent records, and includes high-label fused and bridged examples with unspecified configuration.
transferable_gaps.gap: Valence-valid ring construction is not accompanied by evidence of three-dimensional or synthetic feasibility.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need a distinction between aromatic-ring topology, ring strain or geometry, and macrocycle construction instead of treating parsing success as a complete feasibility certificate. These are different questions and the present audit proves neither universal impossibility nor synthesizability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The Child explores 1869 typed and 1222 generic nonempty scaffolds across 4350 optimizer records, yet one session has a single typed scaffold across its 29 highest-label records. Other sessions retain 14 or 15 typed scaffolds in the same-size high subset, so universal scaffold collapse is not supported.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad exploration does not consistently translate into multiple distinct structural families among the highest observed labels within a session.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic question is how to retain chemically distinct families when the current session supports them, while distinguishing genuine skeleton changes from substituent variants. Scaffold counts and count-fingerprint similarity should use explicit denominators and fragment exclusions; neither is evidence by itself that increased diversity improves the endpoint.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
